newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Ex-RBA gov Fraser says RBA gold sell-down sensible.
newsitem.headline: Ex-RBA gov Fraser says RBA gold sell-down sensible.

text.p: Former Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) governor Bernie Fraser said on Friday the Reserve Bank of Australia's (RBA) decision to sell two thirds of its gold reserves was a sensible portfolio adjustment.
Asked at a building industry luncheon about his thoughts on the RBA's decision, Fraser said: "At this point in time it seems to me to be a sensible portfolio adjustment."
Fraser said if the RBA believed inflation was under control worldwide then the prospect was the price of gold would fall further because gold was an asset that had virtually no return.
"If you hold those sorts of views then it is a sensible portfolio decision. It is clearly better to reinvest those funds in income generating assets," he said.
The RBA announced two weeks ago that it had sold 167 tonnes of gold, or two-thirds of its reserves, news that helped push the precious metal to 12-year lows on world markets.
